backup.dirHint: Once a default backup directory is set, "One-click Backup" writes there directly without asking for a location each time.
backup.dirUnset: Not set (a location picker will appear when backing up)
backup.keepLimitSuffix: (1–100). The oldest backups beyond the limit are pruned automatically after each backup.
backup.emptyWithDir: No backup files in the backup directory yet
backup.restoreHintBefore: Restoring from a backup file will
backup.restoreHintAfter: (destructive). The current data is backed up automatically to the app data directory first; the app restarts automatically after a successful restore.
backup.autoSwitchLabel: When enabled, checks every 24 hours and backs up automatically when data has changed
backup.autoNeedDir: Auto backup takes effect once a backup directory is set
backup.backupHint: Packs the entire ledger (accounts, transactions, budgets, investment holdings, scheduled transactions and all other data) into a single backup file. UI preferences such as theme and default currency are not included.

location.title: Data Location
location.hint: Directory where the ledger database lives. After a change, the app automatically migrates the existing database to the new location on next startup; the files at the old location are kept permanently as a safety net. Restoring the default follows the same flow.
location.fallbackBody: The configured location is unavailable: {reason}. The app has fallen back to the default location automatically; the original database is untouched where it was. You can change the location again or keep things as they are.
location.pendingBody: New location: {dir}. The database migrates automatically on next startup; until then data keeps being written to the current location.
location.adoptBody:
A ledger database (ledger.db) already exists in the target directory.

Adopting it uses that database as the active data; cancelling abandons this change (nothing is modified). The database at the original location is kept after adopting.
location.committed: Change saved; the migration takes effect on next startup

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.hint: Enable file-level encryption for the ledger database: the database and its backups on disk can no longer be read by arbitrary tools. Enabling is a one-step automatic whole-database conversion; on failure the original database stays untouched.
encryption.enabledBody: The current ledger database is encrypted. Enter the master passphrase at every startup to unlock.
encryption.warnBody: You will need the master passphrase to unlock at every startup; the passphrase is never stored and cannot be recovered — losing it means the data can no longer be read (you may reset to a brand-new empty database; the old one is kept as an encrypted copy). The app restarts automatically after conversion.
encryption.mismatch: The two entries do not match
encryption.confirmBody: The whole ledger database will be converted to an encrypted database (do not close the app during conversion); the app restarts automatically afterwards. Continue?
encryption.okToast: Encryption enabled; the app will restart shortly

msg.autoStateFailed: Failed to load auto backup state: {msg}
msg.pruneNotNeeded: Nothing to prune: backup count is within the limit
msg.pruneConfirm: This will delete the oldest {n} backup(s), which cannot be undone. Continue?
msg.restoreConfirm:
Restoring will replace all current data and cannot be undone.

The current data is backed up automatically before restoring; the app restarts automatically after a successful restore.
msg.restoreToPlaintextWarn: The current database is encrypted: restoring this plaintext backup will leave the data unencrypted; the app starts as a plaintext database after restart.
msg.restoreToEncryptedWarn: This backup is encrypted: after restoring, the database becomes encrypted and the master passphrase of that backup is required to unlock on the next start.
msg.restorePassphraseHint: Enter the master passphrase of that backup
msg.restoreOk: Restored (schema v{version}); the app will restart shortly

search.title: Pinyin search data
search.hint: Pinyin-initial search relies on derived pinyin data of transaction notes. Upgrades or interrupted backfill may leave a backlog; Repair fills the whole backlog and reports the result (rows filled / converged / failure reason). Safe to run repeatedly.

report.doneBody: Pinyin data has converged (backlog cleared); pinyin search is fully restored.
report.noopBody: Pinyin data has already converged (0 rows filled this run).
report.notConvergedBody: Some backlog remains. You can run Repair again; search never misses results during backlog.

scheduled.title: Auto Execution
scheduled.switchLabel: Automatically post due installments when enabled
scheduled.body1: When enabled, the app checks every 10 minutes while running and automatically posts due installments, with transaction dates faithfully taken from the planned dates; failed installments stay manual for retry, and paused or cancelled plans are untouched. Auto execution should be enabled on one machine only.
scheduled.body2: This switch is a per-device preference: it does not migrate with backup or restore, and stays off by default on a new machine or after restoring a backup.
